content.title: About
content.content: Tilapia is a freshwater fish from the cichlid family, widely farmed in aquaculture. Grilled, it has a delicate, slightly sweet flavor and a firm yet tender texture. Tilapia is often used in salads, rice dishes, and as a light source of protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tilapia is one of the fastest‑growing farmed fish, reaching market size in 6‑8 months.
The species tolerates a wide range of water conditions, including low oxygen levels.
Its mild taste makes it an excellent canvas for marinades and spices.
Globally, over 5 million tonnes of tilapia are produced each year, making it one of the most popular fish species.
Tilapia can thrive in water temperatures from 15 °C to 30 °C.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Tilapia is a lean fish, suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant and helps maintain immune health.

items.title: Provides essential minerals
items.content: Tilapia supplies phosphorus, potassium and magnesium, important for bone and muscle health.

items.title: Water quality control
items.content: In some regions tilapia may be raised in water with higher contaminant levels; choose products from reputable sources.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: People allergic to seafood may react to tilapia as well.

items.title: Omega‑6 fatty acids
items.content: Tilapia contains more omega‑6 than omega‑3 fatty acids, so balance the diet with other omega‑3 sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Grilled tilapia pairs well with lemon, herbs, garlic, or pesto sauce. It can be sliced for salads, added to pasta, rice dishes, or used in sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh tilapia in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in plastic film, for up to 2 days. Frozen fillets keep at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Discard if it develops an off‑odor.
